newsitem.title: UK: Amersham soars to record on Pharmacia rumour.
newsitem.headline: Amersham soars to record on Pharmacia rumour.

text.p: Shares in British science and technology group Amersham International Plc soared to record levels on Friday amid strong rumours that it was preparing to merge with Pharmacia & Upjohn's Biotech subsidiary.
Both Amersham and Pharmacia & Upjohn declined to comment on reports in the Swedish press that Amersham officials had conducted a due diligence examination of biotech two weeks ago.

However, the markets were clearly giving credit to the rumours. Shares in Amersham jumped 102-1/2 pence to 1405 pence in early trading, their highest-ever level, while in Stockholm shares in Pharmacia rose two Swedish crowns to 264.

Speculation that Amersham could be interested in Biotech has been growing in recent weeks. Pharmacia recently classed the business as an "investment holding," leading analysts to believe it would divest it when a suitable opportunity arose.

Industry observers said the two companies would make a strong fit. Amersham's life sciences division has a growing position making and supplying complex testing systems and molecules for drug discovery.
Pharmacia Biotech is the world's leading developer and supplier of drug assay systems for biotechnology research.
The drug assay business is emerging from a difficult period after cutbacks on health budgets and a series of high profile mergers in the industry reduced spending on technology.

One analyst who asked not to be identified said the main interest would be in how the two companies chose to combine the businesses. He said it was possible that P&U would retain its stake in a combined business, with Amersham gaining overall management control.
Pharmacia Biotech had sales of $439 million in 1996.
Amersham is due to announce full-year results on June 10.
